Share in Chat Share article Facebook X (Twitter) Copy Link Copied WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte — the first Philippine public official to be impeached twice by the House of Representatives — began at 2 pm on Monday, July 6.
There are four articles of impeachment against Duterte involving alleged misuse of confidential funds, unexplained wealth, bribery of Department of Education officials, and grave threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his family.
Only 21 out of 24 senator-judges are physically present. Senator Bato dela Rosa remains in hiding as he faces an International Criminal Court arrest warrant over Rodrigo Duterte’s drug war, Senator Jinggoy Estrada has been detained and suspended in connection with a plunder case, and Senator Rodante Marcoleta surrendered to authorities as he also faces a plunder case.
On this page, we bring you the latest updates, analyses, videos, and photos as the trial of the Vice President unfolds.
House prosecutor Terry Ridon dismisses Vice President Sara Duterte’s remark on “corporate layering” involving Gencorp and Metro City Chow Foods Corporation as a mere excuse, during a press briefing on October 20, 2026.

Share in Chat Share article Facebook X (Twitter) Copy Link Copied Oct 14, 2026 10:54 AM PHT Sara Duterte’s defense team may seek dismissal of remaining impeachment article – lawyer Rappler.com Constitutional lawyer and law professor Lulu Reyes says the defense team of Vice President Sara Duterte may make a major move before the impeachment trial resumes on November 9, potentially seeking a mistrial or filing a demurrer to evidence.
The possible moves could challenge the prosecution’s reliance on financial forensic analyst Alexander Cabrera’s findings, which the defense claims are based on false assumptions.

Rappler multimedia reporter Sundy Locus reports on the defense’s objections, the court’s ruling, and the revised November trial schedule.

Share in Chat Share article Facebook X (Twitter) Copy Link Copied Oct 13, 2026 6:05 PM PHT Impeachment court lifts sub judice rule on withdrawn charges vs Sara Duterte Sundy Locus The Senate impeachment court on Tuesday, October 13, lifted the sub judice rule on three withdrawn impeachment articles against Vice President Sara Duterte, allowing the parties to publicly discuss the dropped charges.
The decision drew objections from lead defense counsel Sheila Sison, who warned that abandoning Rule 18 midway through the trial could undermine the integrity of the proceedings.
